title: use Statement
concept: The `use` keyword brings module paths into the local scope
why: Fully qualified paths like `math::geometry::circle::area()` are verbose and repetitive. The `use` statement shortens these paths so you can call `area()` directly. This reduces visual noise, makes code intent clearer, and follows the principle that frequently-used names should be short.
theory: The `use` statement creates a local binding that maps a module path to a shorter name. It supports absolute paths (from the crate root) with `::` prefix and relative paths without. You can import specific items (`use math::add`), entire modules (`use math`), or rename imports with `as` (`use math::geometry as geo`). XIOM resolves `use` at compile time — there is zero runtime cost. Wildcard imports (`use math::*`) are available but discouraged except in test modules.
tips: Place all `use` statements at the top of the file
Use `as` to disambiguate names from different modules
Avoid `use module::*` — it makes origin of names unclear
common_mistakes: Importing from a private module — the import itself is allowed but access isn't
Shadowing a local name with an import
Using `use` inside a function body (it must be at module level)
